quest.title: Pride and Prejudice
quest.description: While stopping by Gandharva Ville, Ilyas managed to recover his memories. It's now time to follow him to Siraj's hideout.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x775, Primogem x60, Mora x53900, Guide to Ingenuity x5, Hero's Wit x6, Mystic Enhancement Ore x12

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: This is the place.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's so well-hidden, but there's nothing spooky about it. Hm, let's go inside and take a look!

talks.objective: Continue to explore the research base

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Weird, it's bigger on the inside than Paimon imagined. Are you sure it's still a work in progress?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ilyas, do you remember this place? ...Huh? Uh... Ilyas? Where'd he go?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: I don't sense him nearby.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Did he get separated from us? Should we wait here or turn around and look for him?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: There's no need for that. Let's keep moving.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uhh, alright. We'll continue in and see if he catches up to us.

talks.objective: Head into the heart of the research base

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: A sudden dizziness sets in, and a scene starts to play in your mind...

dialogues.speaker: Raju
dialogues.text: It's okay, Ilyas. You've done more than enough for me already...

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: I don't understand. Everyone knows that Jani is stealing your research. Why is no one willing to go public with the truth?

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: He shamelessly used your thesis to send in a project application, and whenever the project hits a wall, he asks you for help. Everyone knows what's going on...

dialogues.speaker: Raju
dialogues.text: Do you know how many people are working on that project? If Jani was kicked out because of academic fraud, that'd be the end of the project. Too many people would be affected!

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: But he's obviously taking advantage of you!

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: He throws you the hardest work. After you're done pulling all-nighters, he struts around with your research data and takes credit for it.

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: That's not right! Why are you putting up with this?

dialogues.speaker: Raju
dialogues.text: A lot of people warned me to not say anything, and I think they have a point. This is just how things are. All I want is to graduate without any problems...

dialogues.speaker: Raju
dialogues.text: It's okay. He's at least paying me.

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: Half a year of your time and effort, countless all-nighters, and casual threats and insults — all for a measly 20,000 Mora?

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: He's treating people like cattle...

dialogues.speaker: Raju
dialogues.text: Enough. It's fine. I just need to suck it up and get it done.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: The scene ends there.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's the matter?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I think I saw a glimpse of Ilyas's past.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh? You could read minds this whole time and you never told Paimon!?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Of course not.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: I was also able to see those memories just now. They were probably the ones that leaked out while Ilyas was connecting to the collective consciousness.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Connecting? Collective consciousness?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: It's clear that this place isn't a work in progress. The Hive has long been finished.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: The collective consciousness project is already complete, and Ilyas is now returning to the collective.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So he tricked us?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Not entirely... Keep walking and you'll see why.

talks.objective: Head into the heart of the research base

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: A new scene plays in your mind...

dialogues.speaker: Janaki
dialogues.text: An entire year's worth of work down the drain, and for what? Your reputation? Do you have any idea how many people you've brought down?

dialogues.speaker: Jaap
dialogues.text: You could've played hero any time, so why couldn't you have waited until the project was complete?

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: I don't understand what you guys are saying. Are you saying you don't care that Raju jumped to his death!?

dialogues.speaker: Jaap
dialogues.text: It's a shame, what happened to him. I thought he was stronger than that.

dialogues.speaker: Jaap
dialogues.text: Everyone has been working hard to complete the project. He could have endured for a bit longer, but he chose now of all times to...

dialogues.speaker: Janaki
dialogues.text: In any case, we're done with you. Because of your recklessness, the matra are putting Jani on trial. This project is done for.

dialogues.speaker: Janaki
dialogues.text: None of this affects you at all, but do you know how many people, myself included, needed this project to complete their studies...?

dialogues.speaker: Janaki
dialogues.text: Now, our futures are up in the air. If worst comes to pass, we might not be able to graduate. Do you understand now?

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: I'm sorry.

dialogues.speaker: Janaki
dialogues.text: There's no need for an apology. It's not like I'll accept it, anyway. You'll pay for this.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: The scene ends there.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, you're blanking out again... What did you see this time?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Ilyas...

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Don't jump to conclusions just yet. Save your words for when we see him.

talks.objective: Head into the heart of the research base

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: The scene is much clearer this time, likely because it happened recently...

dialogues.speaker: Pitar
dialogues.text: Ilyas, this is all very strange. Is there really no research group that will take you?

dialogues.speaker: Pitar
dialogues.text: To pass this course, you must complete a paper with other researchers. I know you're a hero for fighting academic fraud, but we can't make exceptions for heroes, now can we?

dialogues.speaker: Pitar
dialogues.text: Maybe you should try to improve your relationship with the other researchers. Getting a reputation for being too unconventional will not stand you in good stead in the long run.

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: ...I understand.
You seem troubled.

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: Who are you?

dialogues.speaker: Siraj
dialogues.text: Ah, where are my manners? My name is Siraj.

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: Siraj... I've heard of you before. Do you need something from me?

dialogues.speaker: Siraj
dialogues.text: The world hates people who don't fit in. I imagine you've had your fair share of trouble.

dialogues.speaker: Siraj
dialogues.text: After you reported Jani for academic fraud, you were ostracized and shunned. Even your family can't understand your actions.

dialogues.speaker: Siraj
dialogues.text: However, I'm working on some research that will help you "merge into a collective." That way, your life won't be so dolorous.

dialogues.speaker: Siraj
dialogues.text: How about it? Want to have a go?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: The scene ends there.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: What did you see?

choices.text: Siraj persuaded Ilyas to join the Hive.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon can't believe it! He really did trick us, that giga jerk!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No, Siraj is the real giga jerk here! Ilyas is just a regular jerk!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh, Paimon's so mad! We're gonna find him, and we're gonna make him explain himself!

talks.objective: Head into the deepest part of the research base

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ilyas!

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: You've come.

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: I intentionally slowed my integration into the collective consciousness because I wanted to see you one last time as Ilyas.

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: And I wanted to apologize to you as him. It was only at Gandharva Ville that the second thing I must do occurred to me: Bring you all here.

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: To throw off the matra and bring Alhaitham to the Hive — that was my task as Siraj Number 36.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Y—You were already Siraj Number 36? But you passed the matra's lie detector test...！

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: Yes, I truly did forget many things during that time, even my identity and assigned responsibilities.

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: However, it's not that I got scared and forgot. I... chose to delete those memories.

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: It's difficult to fool Alhaitham, so I had to create the perfect guise for myself.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: And the best guise is when you believe your own lies.

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: Correct, I only told you that the Hive was incomplete because I had deleted my memories of its completion.

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: It was finished a long time ago. Before I left, I was already living as Number 36. Now, I choose to return to that identity.

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: Only here I can truly be free.

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: That's all I wanted to say. After I enter this room, my consciousness will merge back into the collective. And so, this is goodbye.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Is this your decision?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, the person we know is Ilyas, not Siraj Number 36!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The outside world is painful sometimes, but Paimon doesn't think that's a reason to run away!

dialogues.speaker: Siraj
dialogues.text: Do you need more time to consider, Ilyas?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, who are—

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: That is Siraj.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So you're that giga jerk!

dialogues.speaker: Siraj
dialogues.text: "Giga jerk"... How bold of you. Have I done something to offend you?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You—

dialogues.speaker: Siraj
dialogues.text: I modified Akasha Terminals to allow users to share memories and emotions. Then, I recruited researchers from the Akademiya to build a collective consciousness.

dialogues.speaker: Siraj
dialogues.text: I assigned numbers to everyone and divided the experiment's tasks amongst themselves.

dialogues.speaker: Siraj
dialogues.text: Here, people can live easily and happily without needing to exercise complex mental thought. This is what they have chosen. All I've done is fulfill their wishes.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Y—You're just trying to justify yourself!

dialogues.speaker: Siraj
dialogues.text: Then I ask you: What's the difference between here and the outside?

dialogues.speaker: Siraj
dialogues.text: There are researchers at the Akademiya who engage in dangerous research in extreme environments, while others become idle and listless.

dialogues.speaker: Siraj
dialogues.text: People are so obsessed with "collective will" that even those on the fringes will attempt to fit in after suffering setbacks.

dialogues.speaker: Siraj
dialogues.text: Isn't that right, Ilyas?

dialogues.speaker: Siraj
dialogues.text: There's no need to deny this, as it is fact. It is natural for social creatures to conform.

dialogues.speaker: Siraj
dialogues.text: And the terminus of "conformity" is a collective consciousness, through which even an ordinary bee colony can become a powerful swarm. Replace the bees with humans, and this model becomes even more potent.

dialogues.speaker: Siraj
dialogues.text: Welcome to the Hive, Alhaitham. You once arrogantly denied the merits of this project before the Grand Sage.

dialogues.speaker: Siraj
dialogues.text: A few simple words from you, and my research was consigned to nothingness. Of course, I'm well aware that you don't care about any of this. You don't care about the pain of others.

dialogues.speaker: Siraj
dialogues.text: But I didn't give up. I made my thesis into reality!

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: When we arrived, I noticed many empty rooms in the Hive.

dialogues.speaker: Siraj
dialogues.text: Oh, you noticed that. Then can you guess where their inhabitants are?

dialogues.speaker: Siraj
dialogues.text: The answer is the Akademiya. They're executing another phase of the plan... the plan to install me as a sage.

dialogues.speaker: Siraj
dialogues.text: The collective consciousness links all of us into a single mind, showcasing our individual strengths as we work together. We are able to execute complex undertakings while instantaneously modifying our strategies in response to unexpected situations.

dialogues.speaker: Siraj
dialogues.text: Everything has been proceeding smoothly — you are our biggest obstacle. With you out of the way, I'll use my growing influence to turn the collective consciousness into a legitimate study.

dialogues.speaker: Siraj
dialogues.text: The project will snowball until ultimately, everyone will be part of my Hive. I— no, the Hive will be in control, and it will lead the Akademiya towards a new future.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We won't let you do this!

dialogues.speaker: Siraj
dialogues.text: What can you achieve with mere words? You weren't even able to change Ilyas's mind.

dialogues.speaker: Siraj
dialogues.text: Return to the Hive, Number 36.

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: ...Yes.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, don't go back! Uh... Look, there are lots of people out there worried about you!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And you aren't an outcast. Aren't we your friends?

dialogues.speaker: Siraj
dialogues.text: That's easy for you to say, given that you're travelers. Will you two continue to stay at the Akademiya? When you leave, tragedy will repeat itself.

dialogues.speaker: Siraj
dialogues.text: Return, Number 36. You know as well as I do that comforting words don't make life any easier.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ilyas... Why...?

dialogues.speaker: Siraj
dialogues.text: You two are just as arrogant as Alhaitham.

dialogues.speaker: Siraj
dialogues.text: You think that everyone should be like you and live according to their own truths, but you don't realize that most people simply want easy lives.

dialogues.speaker: Siraj
dialogues.text: I allowed Number 36 to leave the Hive without his memories only because I knew he would eventually return. This proves that I know more about human nature than you do.

dialogues.speaker: Siraj
dialogues.text: Alhaitham, do say a word or two. I will consider them as your last.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: I made those words quite clear a year ago. The model you presented was extremely unstable. No amount of garish packaging will change its fragile nature.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: *sigh* It can't be helped. If you were clever enough to realize those problems, then you would've been aware that the Hive changed when Ilyas returned to this collective consciousness of yours.

dialogues.speaker: Siraj
dialogues.text: What...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's happening...?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: The collective needs motivation to execute its plans, just as machinery requires energy to operate.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: That's why you, as the Overmind, synchronized your hatred of me into the collective, prompting them to create and execute a plan to eliminate me.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: However, when Ilyas returned to the collective, his memories and emotions were shared with the rest of its members. This includes his perception of me.

dialogues.speaker: Thoughts From Memory
dialogues.text: Thanks for that. You know, you don't seem like such a bad person.

dialogues.speaker: Thoughts From Memory
dialogues.text: Strange, isn't it? Why did I have those thoughts at that time?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: This contradicts the hatred you had provided them, and these two differing emotions will give rise to new conflict.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So that's it! Wait, so you knew that Ilyas would return to the Hive?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And then you pretended to keep him around, just to fool Siraj...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wouldn't expect any less from you, Alhaitham! Once the collective consciousness bugs out, we'll take that opportunity to—

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh? Wait, it's back to normal already!?

dialogues.speaker: Siraj
dialogues.text: Alhaitham, I told you: You're too arrogant! Did you really think that your little scheme would be enough to destabilize the Hive?

dialogues.speaker: Siraj
dialogues.text: Ilyas's return had indeed introduced abnormal emotions into the Hive, but such a meager drop cannot give rise to waves.

dialogues.speaker: Siraj
dialogues.text: Your struggle has been in vain, and it's time to end it. Allow me to show you what makes the collective consciousness so formidable...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So many monsters! Where did they come from?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And, something feels off about them...

dialogues.speaker: Siraj
dialogues.text: I also integrated monsters into the collective, though I ranked them last. Even so, they are part of it.

dialogues.speaker: Siraj
dialogues.text: Despite their lack of intelligence, perfect cooperation can be achieved, much like soldiers who have undergone strict training.

dialogues.speaker: Siraj
dialogues.text: Now then, drown in endless waves of monsters. You... you will all pay for your ceaseless arrogance.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, Alhaitham? Uhh... Your plan didn't work, so what do we do now?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: I've already sent my "gift" to the collective. It will take some time for the recipient to receive it.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: You two just need to brace yourselves for the nuisance in front of us.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, all right. Paimon doesn't know how you get so confident, but we'll hold them off for as long as we can!

dialogues.speaker: Siraj
dialogues.text: You see? That is the will of the collective.

dialogues.speaker: Siraj
dialogues.text: Even with the hatred gone, they continue their work. An external anomaly cannot shake the collective's stability.

dialogues.speaker: Siraj
dialogues.text: What's going on...? What's with this sudden influx of information?

dialogues.speaker: Siraj
dialogues.text: Silence! As the Overmind, I command you—

talks.objective: Witness the internal conflict within the Hive

dialogues.speaker: Karwan
dialogues.text: Oh no, oh no... I was involved in all these plans to get rid of the Acting Grand Sage?

dialogues.speaker: Karwan
dialogues.text: What came over me? How could I do something like this...?

dialogues.speaker: Goli
dialogues.text: We were accomplices without knowing it, but I'm afraid that Alhaitham might pressure the matra into giving us heavier sentences.

dialogues.speaker: Goli
dialogues.text: Whether he's the scribe or the Acting Grand Sage, we can't afford to offend him. It seems our future at the Akademiya will be full of uncertainties...

dialogues.speaker: Pouyan
dialogues.text: We can discuss the future later. Leaving the collective left me with a strange sense of guilt.

dialogues.speaker: Pouyan
dialogues.text: I didn't feel anything towards Alhaitham at first since he wasn't well-known. All the opinions I heard about him were negative, though.

dialogues.speaker: Pouyan
dialogues.text: Siraj made us hate Alhaitham, and we blindly accepted that hatred and thought of him as a bad person.

dialogues.speaker: Pouyan
dialogues.text: From how things look, we've done a lot of irrational things.

dialogues.speaker: Karwan
dialogues.text: I guess we're getting what we deserve. *sigh* ...Could you help us apologize to Alhaitham?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sure, Paimon will help you tell Alhaitham, but whether he chooses to forgive you is up to him.

dialogues.speaker: Karwan
dialogues.text: It's okay. No matter what he chooses, apologizing will make us feel slightly better. If he chooses to remember this, we're prepared for our punishment.

dialogues.speaker: Aarav
dialogues.text: It's time to go.

dialogues.speaker: Goli
dialogues.text: *sigh* Let's go.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So... were they all duped?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We can ask Alhaitham about that later.

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: ...Looks like I can't exist as Siraj Number 36, yet my life as Ilyas goes on.

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: When I was at Gandharva Ville, I thought about whether I should just come forward with the truth.

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: But... I didn't have the courage then.

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: So in the end, I lost my sense of justice, but I also wasn't able to conform.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ilyas...

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: Don't be sad. I'm the one who deceived you.

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: However, I didn't come out of this completely empty-handed. The moment the Hive collapsed, an idea popped into my head.

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: I realized that the "collective" I was always trying to fit into wasn't as powerful as I had imagined.

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: Understanding that gave me courage somehow... Perhaps one day, I can be just like Alhaitham and not care about what anyone else thinks.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You can do it! Paimon believes in you.

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: Thanks. Well, I should get going. I'm one of the primary suspects in the case, so I'll have to receive my due punishment.

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: Can you keep this a secret from my parents and my sister? I just don't want them to worry.

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: Also, please apologize to Alhaitham for me. Goodbye, you two.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: All the test subjects have been taken away.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I'll have my subordinates seal the place, retrieve all documentation, and destroy the system.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Are you two hurt? I brought bandages and hemostatics.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's fine! Whew, just a little tired.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Get some rest. Alhaitham is probably waiting for you at the entrance. Go see him when you're done here.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Watch out for any of Siraj's associates who might still be in hiding. If you encounter anything you can't take care of, come find me at the Akademiya.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay! You stay safe too, Cyno!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's go meet up with Alhaitham!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The Hive... shut down?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's over.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What happened just now?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Members of a collective consciousness are more likely to reach a consensus because of their shared memories and emotions.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: For example, Ilyas did have differing perceptions, but he ultimately followed the collective consciousness's judgment.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: However, this system is far from perfect. Based on this logic, the collective consciousness will generate an intractable diffusion effect upon encountering negative emotions.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Selfish desires...

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: The disturbance that Ilyas caused wasn't for naught. It made the collective question the Overmind.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Setbacks in the plan further amplify doubt, which diminishes the Overmind's influence. This inevitably causes the collective to generate negative emotions.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Apprehension, disappointment, panic, avarice... These negative emotions can be very well hidden, as humans generally do not share completely transparent channels of communication.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: But in the Hive, where there are no secrets, negativity can spread like a tidal wave. Of course, what I said to Ilyas was the trigger for all of this.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: A few words were enough. Believe in the power of words, Siraj.

dialogues.speaker: Siraj
dialogues.text: You were already thinking of a way to destroy the collective consciousness, even back then...

dialogues.speaker: Siraj
dialogues.text: You knew that Ilyas was the bait all along? But how did you know? Since when?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: I knew it from the moment I saw him.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Moreover, I've never looked down on you. My opinion of you has always been objective.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: You have a naive view towards the concepts of collective consciousness and human evolution, but you are intelligent and disciplined.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: You would never let a test subject escape. Mistakes like that are beneath you, and you also won't leave any mistake without a resolution.

dialogues.speaker: Siraj
dialogues.text: Hahaha... I never thought I'd hear those words come from you, but if you're saying that out of sympathy, spare me.

dialogues.speaker: Siraj
dialogues.text: I know very well that you've never viewed me as an equal. When you were with us, you always had a distant look in your eyes.

dialogues.speaker: Siraj
dialogues.text: You don't need to hide it. I know it better than anyone else — the arrogance that comes with being a genius. Nobody likes being treated like that!

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Your perspective is entirely born from your habitual way of looking at things.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: From your perspective, you probably think I'm like you: Someone who doesn't "fit in." However, I've never placed myself on a pedestal.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: I just want to distance myself from meaningless noise and look at everything objectively.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: On the other hand, you have failed to come to terms with who you truly are. You care too much about winning and how others perceive you.

dialogues.speaker: Siraj
dialogues.text: You mean to say that... I'm the arrogant one here?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Is that not so? Arrogant, and emotionally fragile.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: You view people as a simple, mediocre collective, while you regard me as "one of your kind."

dialogues.speaker: Siraj
dialogues.text: Regardless, I have lost. You can take me back to the Akademiya to stand trial.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: You will stand trial, yes, but arresting people isn't in my job description.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: I'm just an ordinary staff member. I believe it is the General Mahamatra's duty to escort you away.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Cyno! What are you doing here?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I followed the symbols. Looks like things have already been settled.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Symbols?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: I left a simple picture in my letter to him, and I made several similar symbols on the way here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, what do you mean you left a letter...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ohhh, Paimon remembers! When Paimon first saw you, Aarav said that you had left a letter for Cyno!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So you really did know that something was up with Ilyas from the start! Argh, you lied to us, too!

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: It'd be best if you didn't spout nonsense. I never employed any mode of trickery on you.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: By the way, I came across some information at the Akademiya a few days ago. If you practice the method discussed therein, your vision may improve. Do you need it?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Seriously? This guy...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, by the way Cyno, Paimon heard that Siraj sent more people to the Akademiya. We can't let those jerks get away!

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Don't worry. The matra have started screening suspicious persons, and we've already arrested many of Siraj's associates.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: This was likely one factor that caused the Hive's consciousness to waver. Everything went as you predicted, Alhaitham.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Good. Hm, seems like the interesting part is already over. I'll leave the arrests to you all.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: See you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And off he goes... *sigh* There still are a lot of test subjects here, so let's stick around for a while.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: The matter's settled. We can return now.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: I actually thought it would've been settled sooner. This took much longer than I expected.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Judging by your faces, it seems like you two still have some questions.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: I respect your curiosity, but I'm off the clock now, so I'm not going to field any questions.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey! We're not your colleagues!

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: ...You couldn't tell that was an excuse just now?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What? Are you kidding me?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You're not leaving today until you explain what happened back at Siraj's secret base!

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: See ya.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ahhh! Hold it right there!

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: Are you done? Your behavior is reminding me of some other people.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Stop changing the subject!

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: It's too much of a hassle to explain everything from the top... You know what? Come with me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh? Where to?

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: You'll know when we get there.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is this... your home?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Yes.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Pfft... What's with you all of a sudden, being all polite and inviting us over?
Ah, you're back. Quick, come help me see if this painting's all straightened... Huh? Who are they!?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Stop making a fuss. They're obviously guests.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: You're... not from the Akademiya, are you?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: No, we're not.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's sure she's seen you before... Huh!? You're the person from that time, in that one place!

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Wait, what? How do you know me!? Oh no, oh no, do people know that I live here...?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: What? You're embarrassed only now of all times?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, you guys are roommates!

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Yes, yes, we are, but keep that to yourselves! Please don't tell anyone else!

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: I keep a few books on collectives and the subconscious here at home. I'll get them. You all chat in the meantime.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, hey!

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Hey! You're leaving, just like that? What's the deal, Alhaitham!?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Sorry, I know we've only just met but I have to ask... Are you, um... You wouldn't happen to be actors that Alhaitham hired to pretend to be his friends, would you?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... what?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Guess not. I've never seen him invite friends home before, so please excuse my surprise. You guys get it, right? You know, with his temperament and stuff...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But... aren't you friends with him?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: ...Uh... I wouldn't say "friends," exactly...

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Okay, well, we used to be. But we're not anymore.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (Huh?)

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Don't worry about it. My name is Kaveh. I'm sorry to have met you under these circumstances. Anyway, please don't say anything about me living here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You seem like you got a lot going on... So maybe some Mora will make Paimon shut up.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Are you serious!? How could you... Ugh, of course — you're Alhaitham's friends!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What!? That was a normal response! You exposed your own weakness!

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Still... Why do you have to treat me like he does?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Judging by the deafening din coming from the living room, you all must be getting along quite well.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Hmph, entertain your own friends, why don't you?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: I'll leave the books here.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You skim through a few pages, but its contents are too esoteric and difficult to understand...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, Paimon's dizzy from reading... This is way too complicated... Why don't we just ask questions instead?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon wants to know... Uh... Oh, how did you know about the collective consciousness's weakness?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: A year ago, Siraj presented his thesis to the Grand Sage, who offhandedly asked for my opinion. I actually responded with two lines of reasoning.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: The first, as I've already said, was that his research was on human evolution, a subject prohibited by the Akademiya.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: The second was that I thought the direction of his research was too extreme, but his approach too conservative.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, that's too conservative? He built such a large lab, gathered all those people, and even tried to get rid of you!

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: One way to stabilize a collective consciousness is to remove the test subjects' humanity altogether.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: The optimal solution to achieve collective consciousness is to focus solely on the Overmind and treat the other test subjects as tools.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's way too dangerous! Y—You're not seriously considering that, are you? 'Cause uh...

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: I'm merely stating the facts. If Siraj had done that, I would've felt his work to be just as senseless.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: It's impossible for any species to evolve overnight, and humans without their humanity cannot be called humans.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: That's why the Akademiya prohibited research into human evolution — most research of this kind tends to run contrary to evolution.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, Paimon gets it now.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Hah, that's rich coming from you. If humans aren't humans without their humanity, then you'll probably evolve into some other species in another decade, I wager?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: What about you? Are you going to devolve into a fungus?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: At least I'd be a fungus with empathy.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Sorry for eavesdropping, but what happened to you guys? Are you in trouble?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sort of. We encountered a strange researcher that had it out for us...

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: ...Are you all okay?

choices.text: To be more precise, they had it out for Alhaitham.

response.speaker: Kaveh
response.text: Huh, so that's how things went...

response.speaker: Kaveh
response.text: *sigh* Such is life. If only he'd known, Alhaitham could have stayed indoors today, and the whole thing could have been avoided. Right?

response.speaker: Kaveh
response.text: Plus, he could have helped me with the housework for once. See those books? They've been sitting there waiting for someone to sort through them for an age. If you're not gonna read them, tidy them away! They don't belong there!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah... Uh...

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: Can you feel the awkwardness in the air? I hope you're aware of your lack of conversational skills.

response.speaker: Kaveh
response.text: Oh, so the pot's calling the kettle black, is he? Hmph, well, having said all that, are you okay?

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: I'm doing quite well — much better than that painting you're trying to hang on the wall.

response.speaker: Kaveh
response.text: You...! You don't understand anything! Stop criticizing my taste in decoration!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Kaveh seems to be upset again...)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon can't tell which of them is more problematic... Let's just get this over with and leave...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I blame your curiosity, Paimon...

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: You whisper very loudly.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, um... Yeah, Paimon's been told that...

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: Do you have any more questions?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let Paimon think... Oh, uh, by the way, the other researchers apologized to you. They hope that you can forgive them.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: I bear them no ill will. More accurately, I don't really care about what they think of me.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: To some extent, they were also fooled by Siraj. The matra will take this into account at their trials.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ilyas also said that he wanted to tell us the truth at Gandharva Ville, but he didn't have the courage.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: He apologized to you, too.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: It doesn't matter. I never considered asking him to come forward with the truth.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: Judging from his experiences, he's more courageous than the average person. There's no need to lay even more criticism on him. Criticizing the brave only shows how weak you yourself are.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: I'm going for dinner in ten minutes, so I'll field one last question.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon doesn't have any more questions. How about you?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What were you actually interested in, Alhaitham?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh yeah, that's a good question.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You only started investigating with the matra at the Akademiya because you were interested in something, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But after meeting Siraj, it didn't seem like you were interested in him or his experiment...

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: I had no interest in him personally, but I was curious as to why so many people were willing to form a collective consciousness with him.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: I now understand the reason.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Something to do with the current atmosphere at the Akademiya, I suppose?

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: Correct. The fall of the sages and the shutdown of the Akasha Terminals deeply affected the Akademiya.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: The fact that Siraj's project attracted so much interest despite not being approved speaks to the lack of research projects as of late.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: As the Acting Grand Sage, I'll have to figure something out.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: In addition, what happened to Ilyas is worth our attention. Reporting academic fraud was the right thing to do. He didn't deserve the outcome that he had received.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon understands now! You're pretty serious when it comes to work, huh?

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: I think "minimum viable seriousness" is a more apt description. I'll do my best to take care of this mess until my resignation is approved.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, your resignation?

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: Yes. I've already submitted my resignation to the Akademiya. Soon, I'll resign as the Acting Grand Sage and go back to being its scribe.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: I don't think Siraj knew about that. If he had waited just a few more days before acting, I would have already resigned.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: What he'd do then wouldn't have been any concern of mine. However, even without my input, his unstable model would have collapsed for some other reason, so it makes no difference.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But... why do you wanna resign?

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: I'm not suited to be a sage, nor do I want to be one. The official process to select the new sages is already underway, but this process is long and takes far too much time.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: If I serve as Acting Grand Sage for too long, the position might become permanent. That would be troublesome. This job isn't something I want to spend the rest of my life doing.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You have a pretty clear direction for yourself.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: It's important to keep your priorities straight. Well, it's about time. You two should grab some dinner, as well.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, now that you say that, Paimon's kinda hungry! See ya! We're gonna grab some yummies!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Goodbye!

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: See ya.

choices.text: We just happened to be there.

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: (I must... return... to the Hive.)

dialogues.speaker: Member of the Collective Consciousness
dialogues.text: (I just have to stay here... Just follow the collective...)

dialogues.speaker: Member of the Collective Consciousness
dialogues.text: (No need to choose, no responsibilities. Life has become so easy, just like that...)

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: (Sheep without a shepherd.)

dialogues.speaker: Aarav
dialogues.text: (As expected of Mahamatra Cyno...)

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: (Was I wrong?)

dialogues.speaker: Karwan
dialogues.text: (What have I done?)

dialogues.speaker: Goli
dialogues.text: (He's sure to get revenge on us!)

dialogues.speaker: Pouyan
dialogues.text: (Pride and prejudice are frightening...)
